title: The Retailer-Exclusive Shake and the Real Bottle
lessons: The player encounters PRIME's Target-exclusive, Pop-Tarts-flavored Ultra-Filtered Shake instead of the original hydration bottle.
The player already knows PRIME but sees unfamiliar packaging and checks the brand site to make sure the bottle is legitimate.

text: You find a shake carton wedged into the cooler where the hydration bottles usually are.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: "Frosted Strawberry." A protein shake tastes like a Pop-Tart now?

entry-first-2.speaker: PRIME
text: 32 grams of protein wearing a toaster pastry's face. Frosted Chocolate Fudge too, if strawberry's not your thing.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: And I can only get it here?

entry-first-4.speaker: PRIME
text: Target only. My name and Pop-Tarts' on the same carton, nowhere else on earth. You came in for a bottle. I'm seeing if you'll follow me to the dairy case.

choice-first.speaker: PRIME
text: You're still holding it. Cold hand yet?

choices.text: A breakfast pastry as a protein shake flavor is unhinged, in a good way.
Locking it to one retailer feels like a stunt more than a shake.
I wanted a drink, not a Pop-Tarts crossover event.

first-1.speaker: PRIME
text: Thank you. Restraint has never tested well on me.

first-2.speaker: PRIME
text: It's a stunt. It's also a shake. Half the comments said genius, half said gross, and both halves showed up at Target. I checked.

first-3.speaker: PRIME
text: Then buy the one thing you came for. I can handle a smaller cart. I'll be annoyed about it, but I can handle it.
You know PRIME. This bottle's label looks slightly off. There's a page on the brand site for exactly this.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Why does this bottle look wrong?

entry-return-2.speaker: PRIME
text: Don't drink it yet. Check it.

entry-return-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: You have a whole page for that?

entry-return-4.speaker: PRIME
text: Country, size, label, formula, flavors. When you get this big, fakes show up. I'd rather you find out from my page than from your stomach.

choice-return.speaker: PRIME
text: Well? Real or not?

choices.text: I like that I can check it myself.
The fact that I need to verify a sports drink is wild.
If I have to investigate a bottle, I'm buying something else.

return-1.speaker: PRIME
text: Good. Trust the list and the stores on it. A random bottle with my logo isn't me until the page says so.

return-2.speaker: PRIME
text: I know. Needing a verification page is not a victory lap.

return-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Finally, humility.

return-2-2.speaker: PRIME
text: Do not get used to it.

return-3.speaker: PRIME
text: Reasonable. A sports drink shouldn't need detective work. Mine does, sometimes. That's the cost of being copied.
